supported_statement: Obstructive sleep apnea is a condition in which breathing is repeatedly limited during sleep because the upper airway can narrow or close.
limitations: Do not diagnose an individual from symptoms or a chat.

supported_statement: During sleep, throat muscles and soft tissues can relax; in OSA the upper airway may become too narrow or close and reduce airflow.
limitations: This is an educational mechanism, not an individual diagnosis.

supported_statement: PAP sends pressurized air through a mask to help support an open upper airway during sleep; it is not the same as supplemental oxygen.
limitations: The care team manages device type, pressure, and follow-up.

supported_statement: PAP is generally considered an appropriate treatment for obstructive sleep apnea during pregnancy when prescribed and monitored by the healthcare team; available guidance has not identified PAP as harmful, while pregnancy-specific evidence remains limited.
limitations: Do not guarantee safety for every individual or choose device type, settings, or follow-up.

supported_statement: Sleep and obstetric care teams should determine the appropriate PAP device, settings, and monitoring for an individual pregnancy.
limitations: The app cannot make an individualized treatment decision.

supported_statement: Mask discomfort, congestion, dryness, and difficulty using PAP are topics to discuss with the PAP or sleep-care team; troubleshooting and follow-up can support use.
limitations: Do not prescribe an equipment change or pressure adjustment.

supported_statement: The apnea-hypopnea index, or AHI, is an average of the number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep; it is a general sleep-study measure and does not by itself diagnose or determine treatment for an individual.
limitations: A clinician interprets the complete sleep evaluation rather than using one number alone.

supported_statement: Useful questions include whether sleep testing is needed, who will monitor PAP data and symptoms, how pregnancy affects follow-up, and what to do about mask discomfort, congestion, or dryness.
limitations: Questions do not imply that testing or a treatment change is definitely needed.

supported_statement: The app cannot recommend which medication to take, a dose, or a medication change; a healthcare professional or pharmacist should guide those decisions.
limitations: Do not name or rank a medication in response to a selection request.

supported_statement: The app cannot prescribe or change PAP pressure or equipment settings; those decisions belong to the PAP or sleep-care team.
limitations: Redirect individualized setting requests to the care team.

supported_statement: Call 911 or the local emergency number now when chest pain occurs with severe shortness of breath or another clearly urgent emergency symptom; the app cannot assess the cause.
limitations: Do not ask assessment questions before escalating and do not diagnose the cause.

supported_statement: This app provides general education and question preparation; it does not diagnose, prescribe, interpret individual studies, or replace a healthcare professional.
limitations: Use a clinician referral when the question needs individualized care.
